files.powerblind_smartmeter_readings.csv: Main time-series dataset, one row per consumer-day
files.powerblind_consumer_labels.csv: Consumer-level metadata: ground-truth label, subtype, anomaly window

columns.kwh: Daily energy consumption in kWh (NaN during communication failure gaps)
columns.current_a: Average daily current draw (Amps), derived from power/voltage/PF
columns.comm_flag: True if this day was affected by a communication failure event
columns.label: Ground truth class: Normal, Theft, FaultyMeter, CommFailure
columns.anomaly_subtype: Specific sub-type of anomaly (see taxonomy below), 'None' if Normal

theft_subtypes.T1_PartialReduction: Constant gamma-factor reduction of true consumption (classic tampering)
theft_subtypes.T2_ZeroConsumption: Meter reports near-zero while consumer continues to use electricity (bypass)
theft_subtypes.T3_RandomReduction: Time-varying random reduction factor applied per day
theft_subtypes.T4_ByPassMeter: Flatlined low reporting regardless of actual usage pattern
theft_subtypes.T5_ReverseTamper: Usage pattern reversed/smeared to obscure peak load timing

faulty_meter_subtypes.F1_StuckAt: Meter reports same frozen value for an extended period
faulty_meter_subtypes.F2_Drift: Gradual linear drift away from true consumption (calibration decay)
faulty_meter_subtypes.F3_NoiseSpike: Random large-magnitude spikes due to sensor malfunction
faulty_meter_subtypes.F4_UnderRegister: Consistent fixed-percentage under-reporting due to miscalibration

notes: Base normal consumption patterns are calibrated using real-world statistical parameters (seasonal amplitude, weekly residential/commercial cycles, base load ranges) consistent with structures reported in Irish CER and SGCC literature.
Anomalies are injected synthetically using formulas adapted from published electricity theft detection literature (e.g. Jokar et al. 2016 attack taxonomy; SGCC Wide & Deep CNN paper).
Random seed fixed at 42 for reproducibility.
Designed for multi-class classification (Normal / Theft / FaultyMeter / CommFailure) plus theft/fault/comm sub-type classification for explainability (XAI) modeling.
